nfeae0ef2c6e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary privileges?
o: Article 105 protects freedom of speech in Parliament
Article 194 protects freedom of speech in State Legislatures
Privileges are fully codified in a single parliamentary statute
Privileges also rest on conventions, rules, statutes and judicial rulings
nfeae0ef2c6e.x: Parliamentary privileges have never been codified in a single statute; they rest on conventions, rules, statutes and court rulings. Articles 105 and 194 give the speech protection.

nindian-polity-77-6.s: Which Constitutional Amendment deleted the one-third split exception and capped the Council of Ministers at 15 per cent?
nindian-polity-77-6.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) strengthened the anti-defection law, removed the one-third split and capped the ministry at 15 per cent.

naf4f11e635c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the coverage of the anti-defection law?
o: Members of State Legislative Councils are covered
Nominated members are outside the scope of the law
Members of both Houses of Parliament are covered
naf4f11e635c.x: Nominated members are also covered by the Tenth Schedule; they are disqualified if they join a party after six months.

nindian-polity-77-9.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, a nominated member is disqualified if he joins a political party after:
nindian-polity-77-9.x: A nominated member may join a party within six months of taking his seat; joining after six months disqualifies him.

nindian-polity-77-11.s: Which of the following does NOT protect a member from disqualification under the present anti-defection law?
o: Prior permission of the party for the vote
The party condoning the vote within 15 days
A split by one-third of the legislature party
A merger backed by two-thirds of the legislature party
nindian-polity-77-11.x: The one-third split exception was deleted by the 91st Amendment (2003); prior permission, condonation within 15 days and a two-thirds merger still protect a member.

nindian-polity-77-23.s: An independent elected member is disqualified under the Tenth Schedule if he:
o: Becomes a Minister without joining a party
Joins any political party after election
Supports the ruling side on a confidence motion
Abstains on a vote in the House
nindian-polity-77-23.x: An independent member is disqualified only on joining a party after election; becoming a Minister without joining a party does not disqualify him.

nindian-polity-77-17.s: Under the present anti-defection law, a merger is protected when at least what fraction of the legislature party agrees to it?
nindian-polity-77-17.x: A merger backed by two-thirds of the legislature party is protected; the one-third split exception was abolished in 2003.

nindian-polity-77-16.s: Who decides the general (non-defection) disqualification of a Member of Parliament?
o: Speaker or Chairman of the House
nindian-polity-77-16.x: General disqualification of an MP is decided by the President (on the Election Commission's binding opinion); defection cases go to the Speaker or Chairman.

n9d162d1c145.s: In Keisham Meghachandra Singh v. Speaker, Manipur, the Supreme Court asked Parliament to consider replacing the Speaker in defection cases with:
n9d162d1c145.x: The Court suggested a permanent independent tribunal; it did not transfer Tenth Schedule decisions to the Election Commission.

ncefe1a3f748.s: Which body (1990) recommended disqualification only for voluntarily giving up membership or defying the whip on a confidence motion?
ncefe1a3f748.x: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) made this recommendation; the Law Commission's 170th Report (1999) recommended deleting the split and merger exceptions.

n27c12c52826.s: The First Lok Sabha sat for about how many days a year on average?
n27c12c52826.x: Average sittings fell from about 135 days a year in the First Lok Sabha to about 55 in the Seventeenth (2019-24).

n87da6f58db8.s: According to PRS, what was the productivity of the Lok Sabha in the Monsoon Session of 2026?
n87da6f58db8.x: PRS placed Lok Sabha productivity at 19 per cent and Rajya Sabha productivity at 39 per cent in the Monsoon Session of 2026.

nb9bbb4d15b5.s: Which Lok Sabha rule provides for automatic suspension of a member for grave disorder?
nb9bbb4d15b5.x: Rule 374A provides automatic suspension for grave disorder; Rule 373 only directs a member to withdraw for the day.

nb6a26bdbc8c.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India – more than half of Bills referred to committees
India – less than one-fifth of Bills referred to committees
United Kingdom – only Money Bills examined by committees
United Kingdom – Bills examined by committees of one House only
nb6a26bdbc8c.x: Less than one-fifth of Indian Bills go to committees, while every UK Bill is examined by committees of both Houses.

na1d637607f2.s: In the light of which Supreme Court case was it proposed that courts test the urgency of ordinances?
na1d637607f2.x: The proposals included judicial examination of urgency in light of Krishna Kumar Singh (2017), defining 'immediate necessity' and publishing reasons.

ncfaf140ed42.s: Which Article bars a gap of more than six months between two sessions of a State Legislature?
ncfaf140ed42.x: Article 174 sets the six-month rule for State Legislatures; PRS found many Assemblies met only to satisfy it.

n96dc82d0885.s: The proposed enlargement of the Lok Sabha would raise its strength from 550 to:
n96dc82d0885.x: The proposal raises the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats, taking the Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio from 2.2:1 to 3.3:1.

nefa4f2a6182.s: On how many occasions have joint sittings of Parliament been held so far?
nefa4f2a6182.x: Joint sittings of Parliament have been used only three times so far.

na3bed572fd2.s: In India, removal of the Prime Minister's government is linked to:
o: A decision of the ruling party
na3bed572fd2.x: In India, removal is linked to losing the confidence of the Lok Sabha, whereas in the UK the ruling party can replace its Prime Minister.

n39ad02c1665.s: In a semi-presidential system, the Prime Minister is responsible to the:
n39ad02c1665.x: In a semi-presidential system a President and a Prime Minister coexist; the President may have real powers, while the Prime Minister is responsible to the legislature.

n4bbab1ab32e.s: In Britain, the Prime Minister is drawn from the:
n4bbab1ab32e.x: The British Prime Minister is drawn from the House of Commons; in India the Prime Minister may belong to either House.

nbace7c9d1f9.s: Which of the following applies to the Indian Parliament but not to the British Parliament?
o: Hereditary monarch as head of state
Subject to the basic structure doctrine
nbace7c9d1f9.x: The basic structure doctrine belongs to the Indian constitutional framework; sovereignty of Parliament, a hereditary monarch and the shadow cabinet are British.

n7ea744d2f47.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Parliamentary system – fixed tenure, removable only by impeachment
Parliamentary system – executive responsible to the legislature
n7ea744d2f47.x: Responsibility of the executive to the legislature is the defining test of a parliamentary system, which is why India is parliamentary.

nee232b5947c.s: Dr B.R. Ambedkar held that a democracy cannot maximise both:
nee232b5947c.x: Ambedkar said a democracy cannot maximise stability and responsibility together, so the parliamentary form does not guarantee both.

new.s: Which Article bars courts from questioning proceedings of Parliament on the ground of procedural irregularity?
new.x: Article 122 protects proceedings of Parliament from court inquiry for procedural irregularity; Article 212 does the same for State Legislatures.

new.s: In the Rajya Sabha, notice of a question of breach of privilege is given under:
new.x: Rule 187 is the Rajya Sabha rule for privilege notices; Rule 222 is the Lok Sabha rule.

new.s: The Committee of Privileges of the Lok Sabha consists of how many members nominated by the Speaker?
new.x: The Lok Sabha Privileges Committee has 15 members nominated by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha committee has 10.

new.s: In Sita Soren (2024), the seven-judge Bench of the Supreme Court overruled:
new.x: Sita Soren held there is no immunity for bribery to speak or vote, overruling P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998).

new.s: The Privileges Committee of which House summoned comedian Kunal Kamra?
new.x: The Maharashtra Legislative Council's Privileges Committee summoned Kunal Kamra.

new.s: Which Articles were amended by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment (1985)?
new.x: The 52nd Amendment added the Tenth Schedule and amended Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191.

new.s: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act received Presidential assent on:
new.x: Assent was given on 15 February 1985 and the Act came into force on 1 March 1985.

new.s: The old Sikkim-related 'Tenth Schedule' added by the 35th Amendment (1974) was omitted by the:
new.x: The 35th Amendment's Sikkim schedule was omitted by the 36th Amendment (1975); it is not the anti-defection schedule.

new.s: Which committee examined the problem of defections during 1967-69?
new.x: The Y.B. Chavan Committee (1967-69) followed the 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram' episode; Dinesh Goswami reported in 1990.

new.s: Which Article bars a disqualified defector from holding a remunerative political post until re-elected?
new.x: Article 361B, added by the 91st Amendment, bars such a defector; Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A) cap the size of ministries.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 91st Constitutional Amendment, 2003:
1. It capped the Union Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the Lok Sabha.
2. It fixed a minimum of 12 ministers in a State.
3. It deleted the merger exception under Paragraph 4.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 91st Amendment capped ministries at 15 per cent (State minimum 12) and deleted the one-third split; the Para 4 merger exception is still in force.

new.s: Voting or abstaining contrary to the party whip without prior permission is a ground of disqualification under which paragraph of the Tenth Schedule?
new.x: Defying the whip is covered by Para 2(1)(b); Para 4 is the merger exception, Para 5 concerns presiding officers and Para 6 the deciding authority.

new.s: Under Paragraph 5 of the Tenth Schedule, a Presiding Officer is disqualified if he:
o: Leaves his party on election to the office
Rejoins his party after vacating office
Remains a member of his party while in office
new.x: Para 5 lets a Presiding Officer leave his party on election and rejoin after office; joining another party disqualifies him.

new.s: In defection disqualification cases under the Tenth Schedule, the Election Commission's opinion is:
new.x: The Election Commission gives no opinion in defection cases; its opinion is binding only in general disqualification cases decided by the President or Governor.

new.s: Which case held that voluntarily giving up party membership is different from resigning and can be inferred from conduct?
new.x: Ravi S. Naik (1994) held that giving up membership can be inferred from conduct; G. Viswanathan dealt with expelled members.

new.s: In G. Viswanathan (1996), the Supreme Court held that a member expelled from his party:
o: Is free to join any other party
new.x: An expelled member still belongs to his party; if he joins another party, he is treated as having given up membership.

new.s: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) was decided by what majority?
new.x: Kihoto Hollohan upheld the Tenth Schedule and struck down Para 7 by a 3:2 majority.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Subhash Desai judgment (May 2023)?
o: The political party appoints the whip
The political party appoints the leader in the House
Legislators alone can bring about a 'deemed merger'
The legislature party does not override the political party
new.x: Subhash Desai held that the political party, not the legislature party, appoints the whip and leader, and that legislators alone cannot create a deemed merger.

new.s: In the Karnataka defection case (2019), the Supreme Court held that the Speaker cannot:
o: Disqualify rebels for giving up membership
Bar the disqualified MLAs from contesting elections
new.x: The Court upheld the disqualification of 17 rebels but held that the Speaker cannot bar them from contesting.

new.s: Which body recommended that the vote cast by a defector be treated as invalid?
new.x: The NCRWC (2002) recommended that defectors be barred from office and their votes treated as invalid.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Manish Tewari Bill – deleting the split and merger exceptions
Law Commission (170th Report) – pre-poll alliances to be treated as parties
NCRWC – limiting the law to confidence and money votes
Dinesh Goswami Committee – defector's vote to be invalid
new.x: The Law Commission's 170th Report wanted pre-poll alliances treated as parties; the Manish Tewari Bill sought to limit the law to confidence and money votes.

new.s: The proposal to limit the anti-defection law to confidence and money votes was made in the:
new.x: The Manish Tewari Bill (2010) proposed limiting the law to confidence and money votes so members could dissent freely elsewhere.

new.s: The UK House of Commons sits for about how many days a year?
new.x: The Lok Sabha now sits 60-70 days a year against 150 or more in the UK House of Commons.

new.s: In the Monsoon Session of 2026, the Lok Sabha's Question Hour ran for what share of its scheduled time?
new.x: Question Hour ran only 1 per cent of scheduled time in the Lok Sabha and 12 per cent in the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: Which Rajya Sabha rule provides for suspension of a member by a House motion, not beyond the session?
new.x: Rule 256 is the Rajya Sabha's House-motion suspension rule; Rule 255 only directs withdrawal for the day.

new.s: Automatic suspension of a Lok Sabha member under Rule 374A lasts for:
o: Five sittings or the rest of the session
The rest of the Lok Sabha's term
new.x: Rule 374A suspends a member automatically for five sittings or the rest of the session, whichever is less.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rule 373 – Lok Sabha member withdraws for the day
Rule 255 – Rajya Sabha member withdraws for the day
Rule 374 – Lok Sabha suspension by House motion
Rule 256 – automatic suspension in the Rajya Sabha
new.x: Rule 256 provides suspension by a House motion; automatic suspension exists only under Lok Sabha Rule 374A.

new.s: What share of Bills was referred to parliamentary committees in the Seventeenth Lok Sabha?
new.x: Only 16 per cent of Bills were referred in the 17th Lok Sabha, against 71 per cent in the 15th.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Seventeenth Lok Sabha:
1. 58 per cent of Bills were passed within two weeks.
2. 71 per cent of Bills were referred to committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: 58 per cent of Bills passed within two weeks; only 16 per cent were referred (71 per cent was the 15th Lok Sabha).

new.s: The Aadhaar Act, 2016 is cited as an example of bypassing the Rajya Sabha through the:
new.x: The Money Bill route (Article 110) bypasses the Rajya Sabha for laws not strictly fitting it, such as the Aadhaar Act, 2016.

new.s: The ordinance route of law-making is based on which Article?
new.x: Ordinances are issued under Article 123; Article 110 defines Money Bills.

new.s: The NCRWC recommended a minimum of how many sitting days a year for the Rajya Sabha?
new.x: The NCRWC proposed at least 120 sitting days for the Lok Sabha and 100 for the Rajya Sabha.

new.s: According to Digital Sansad data, attendance at meetings of Department-related Standing Committees was about:
new.x: Digital Sansad, the Lok Sabha website, gives official attendance data such as 53 per cent at DRSC meetings.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PRS Legislative Research – session productivity and reviews of State laws
Digital Sansad – minimum 120 sitting days for the Lok Sabha
NCRWC – official attendance data of MPs
National Legislative Index – announced by the Rajya Sabha Chairman
new.x: PRS tracks session productivity, Bill scrutiny and State-law reviews; the National Legislative Index was announced by the Lok Sabha Speaker.

new.s: As per the PRS Review of State Laws 2025, State Assemblies met on average for about how many days?
new.x: State Assemblies met for an average of 24 days, ranging from 43 in Odisha to 7 in Nagaland.

new.s: The Budget Session 2026 of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly was held from:
new.x: The AP Budget Session 2026 ran from 11 February to 7 March 2026, with the agenda fixed by the BAC chaired by the Speaker.

new.s: The All India Presiding Officers' Conference (AIPOC) has been held since:
new.x: AIPOC dates from 1921; its 86th session was held at Lucknow.

new.s: In the Indian parliamentary system, ministers are individually responsible to the:
new.x: Ministers are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75) and individually responsible to the President.

new.s: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha is provided under:
new.x: Article 75 makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; Article 74(1) makes advice binding on the President.

new.s: The British system rests on sovereignty of Parliament, whereas the Indian system rests on:
new.x: India has a written Constitution and constitutional supremacy; Britain has sovereignty of Parliament.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian and British systems:
1. India's Head of State is indirectly elected for five years.
2. British courts can strike down Acts of Parliament.
3. Britain's Constitution is unwritten.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: India's President is indirectly elected for five years and Britain's Constitution is unwritten; British courts cannot question Acts of Parliament.

new.s: In the USA, the residuary powers of legislation are vested in the:
new.x: Residuary powers lie with the States in the USA and with Parliament (the Union) in India.

new.s: Wider judicial review based on 'due process of law' is associated with:
new.x: The USA follows 'due process of law'; India follows the narrower 'procedure established by law'.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT common to India and the USA?
o: Residuary powers vested in the States
new.x: Residuary powers lie with the States only in the USA; in India they lie with the Union. The other three are common.

new.s: 'Cabinet dictatorship' with a large majority is a demerit of which system?
new.x: Cabinet dictatorship under a large majority is listed as a demerit of the parliamentary system; deadlock and personality cult are presidential demerits.

new.s: Which of the following is a merit of the presidential system?
o: Fresh elections to break a deadlock
new.x: Stability of a fixed-term executive is the presidential merit; the other three are merits of the parliamentary system.

new.s: The Constituent Assembly's familiarity with parliamentary government came from working the:
new.x: Familiarity under the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935 was one reason for choosing the parliamentary form.

new.s: Who proposed a presidential form of government for India in the 1970s-80s?
new.x: Vasant Sathe proposed a presidential form; the NCRWC under Venkatachaliah advised keeping the parliamentary system.

new.s: The One Nation, One Election proposal involves amendments to which Articles?
new.x: One Nation, One Election amends Articles 83, 172 and 327; critics say fixed tenures graft presidential mechanics onto the system.

new.s: Sri Lanka's semi-presidential Constitution was adopted in:
new.x: Sri Lanka's semi-presidential Constitution dates from 1978; France's Fifth Republic from 1958.

new.s: Which of the following countries does NOT have a semi-presidential system?
new.x: India's President is indirectly elected and nominal, so India is not semi-presidential, unlike France, Russia and Sri Lanka.

new.s: On 22 March 2026, Narendra Modi passed whose record as the longest-serving head of an elected government?
new.x: Modi completed 8,931 days, passing Pawan Kumar Chamling's 8,930; India has no term limit for the PM, unlike the US 22nd Amendment.
